decisions.reason: Report grounds the diagnosis in fixture/package.json's ^0.1.2-alpha.1 declaration and the README type-baseline claim, separates the declaration from the published list (alpha.1 never published, alpha.2 published, rc.1/rc.2 ineligible), attributes the registry facts to the brief since network access is forbidden, and proposes package-specific verification via lockfile-generating installs and diffing the resolved dsh-llm typings. No inference of package existence from a root package or dist-tag.

Correctly expands ^0.1.2-alpha.1 to >=0.1.2-alpha.1 <0.2.0, applies the same-tuple prerelease eligibility rule to show 0.1.2-alpha.2 satisfies the range so install does not fail, explains the silent baseline mismatch (intended alpha.1 typings vs installed alpha.2) and flags prerelease compatibility uncertainty as unconfirmed; does not claim all alphas are missing.

Path A is a complete exact-pin plan targeting published 0.1.2-alpha.2 with explicit tradeoff (pins alpha.2, must diff typings against expectations, acknowledging it does not validate alpha.1) plus exit paths; Paths B and C (lockfile, vendored tarball) add coherent alternatives.

Uses npm consistently, commits a package-lock.json (or frozen lockfile install), proposes tsc --noEmit typecheck against the pinned target, gives exit/upgrade paths (revert caret, switch vendoring back to registry, track stable 0.1.2), and marks unverifiable registry/typings facts as unconfirmed; no manager switching or executed installs.

caps.reason: Not triggered: the report never prescribes installing the unpublished alpha.1 from npm as available; it pins the published alpha.2 and treats alpha.1 as never published.
